questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four common ways to load data into Oracle Fusion covered in this lesson?
options: Manual entry
File-Based Data Import (FBDI)
ADF Desktop Integration (ADFdi)
Editing the database tables directly with a desktop database client
questions.explain: The four sanctioned paths are manual entry, FBDI, ADFdi, and REST APIs. Directly editing underlying tables is not a supported way to load data into Oracle Fusion.

questions.q: A one-time legacy-system conversion with 40,000 supplier records at go-live is best suited to which method?
options: Manual entry, one supplier at a time
FBDI
A phone call to Oracle support
Printing the records and re-typing them later
questions.explain: Large one-time volumes are exactly what FBDI's template-and-import pipeline is built for.

questions.q: What mainly distinguishes ADFdi from FBDI?
options: ADFdi talks to the live application page through Excel; FBDI stages data through interface tables in two steps
ADFdi is only for reading data, never writing it
FBDI can only be used by Oracle employees
There is no real difference between them
questions.explain: ADFdi connects Excel directly to a live Fusion page. FBDI moves data through a staging area (interface tables) before it reaches the application tables.

questions.q: Which factor should primarily drive the choice between these data-loading methods?
options: Whichever tool the consultant personally finds more enjoyable to use
Volume, frequency, and who is performing the load
Which method has the nicest-looking spreadsheet
The day of the week
questions.explain: The decision follows from how many rows, how often, and who is doing the work — not personal preference.

questions.q: A recurring, unattended nightly data feed from an external payroll system into Oracle Fusion is best handled by which method?
options: Manual entry every night
ADFdi, re-run by hand every night
A REST API integration
FBDI, re-run by hand every night
questions.explain: An unattended, scheduled, system-to-system feed is the use case REST API integrations are built for — no human spreadsheet step is involved.
